{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = "/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/sales.csv"
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Inspect the data
print("Data head:")
print(data.head())

print("\nData dtypes:")
print(data.dtypes)

print("\nUnique channels:")
print(data['channel'].unique())

print("\nRevenue sample:")
print(data['revenue'].head())

# Check for QA orders
qa_orders = data[data['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print(f"\nNumber of QA orders: {len(qa_orders)}")

# Check for refunded orders
refunded_orders = data[data['status'] == 'refunded']
print(f"\nNumber of refunded orders: {len(refunded_orders)}")

# Convert revenue to float: remove commas and cast to float
# First, check for any non-numeric strings beyond expected format
print("\nUnique revenue values:")
print(data['revenue'].unique()[:10])  # Show first 10 unique values

# Handle revenue: remove commas and cast to float
# But first, check if there are any malformed values
malformed = data['revenue'].str.contains(r'[^0-9,\.]', na=False)
print(f"\nMalformed revenue entries: {data[malformed]['revenue'].unique()}")

# Replace commas and convert to float
data['revenue_float'] = data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Drop QA orders and refunded orders
data_clean = data[~((data['revenue'] == '999999.99') | (data['status'] == 'refunded'))]

# Recalculate revenue_float for clean data
data_clean['revenue_float'] = data_clean['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Compute total revenue by channel
revenue_by_channel = data_clean.groupby('channel')['revenue_float'].sum().round(2)
print("\nTotal revenue by channel:")
print(revenue_by_channel)

# Identify the channel with the most revenue
max_channel = revenue_by_channel.idxmax()
max_revenue = revenue_by_channel.max()

print(f"\nChannel with highest revenue: {max_channel} with ${max_revenue:,.2f}")"}
